summary: Spec fidelity: the brief's F5 failure path reads 'no source holds a flag-only list naming repo and as; the crate's set is used', while its own F5 paragraph says canon's set is the crate's plus repo and as. The change resolves it as the second (input::OWN_FLAGS_ONLY = [repo, as], flags_only() = those plus atip::flag_only_options(V1_2), and atip.canoncursor.11 asserts the set and that no source names the contract's options); no list of the contract's eight options survives in canon's source (FLAGS_ONLY, INVOCATION and set_invocation are gone, grep). Verified in the real binary: query, finding list, divergence list, export, retrieve and search have limit/cursor/all/fields (retrieve and search: limit) flagOnly true and no fragment schema key of theirs; export --input with limit, cursor, all or fields, and a batch with limit in element 1, answers INPUT_INVALID FLAG_ONLY_KEY at /limit, /cursor, /all, /fields, /1/limit. query, finding list and divergence list take no --input, so F5's input rule has no document path there (the scenarios say so by testing export only). Blast radius: retrieve and search now declare limit flagOnly in docs/cli/canon.cli.json; a consumer of that document that read flagOnly false there sees the change.
